proposals.name: Thunder-Mead
proposals.entry:
Thunder-Mead is made from the honey of the Pyre Bee and occupies an unusual place in Gravosk culture: ceremonial drink, festival staple, and valued material used in several traditional military and industrial preparations.

Different grades are prepared for different purposes. Drinking grades are served from horns at meals and festivals. Other preparations are reserved for armories and Great Bombard crews.

At weddings, certain varieties are briefly ignited as part of the ceremony. At funerals, Thunder-Mead is poured upon the pyre before the mourners drink from the same batch.

Gravosk artillery positions consequently smell unlike those of most armies: burned honey, pine resin, hot iron and smoke.

A common saying is: “If it won’t fire, drink it. If you can’t drink it, fire it.”

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
Pyre-bee colonies across several strategically important valleys have begun disappearing without leaving dead bees behind.

A Drusha experiment produced a concentrated Thunder derivative that burned an unmistakable magenta—the same color now seen in Lumber Maton engines. Neither people publicly discusses the connection.
